title: Tabachnikov's Problem 2 as one named proposition

blocks.tex: Tabachnikov Problem 2 is the proposition that every positive constant or four-vertex cyclic profile is realized by a coherent simple polygon. The definitions and equivalences below connect its window and extremum formulations.

blocks.label: def:tab_problem2
blocks.title: Tabachnikov's Problem 2 at length $n$
blocks.body:
For $n$ with $\mathrm{NeZero}\,n$,
  \[
    \mathrm{TP2}(n) \;:\equiv\;
      \forall \kappa : \mathbb{Z}/n \to \mathbb{R},\
        \operatorname{DiscreteFourVertexPos}(\kappa)
        \Rightarrow \operatorname{RealizesR2}(\kappa) .
  \]
  In words: every positive cyclic curvature word of length $n$ which is
  constant or admits a strict four-vertex window at a positive level is
  realized by a simple moderate-arc Euclidean $n$-gon with those signed
  Menger curvatures.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.TabachnikovProblem2
lean.code:
def TabachnikovProblem2 (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] : Prop :=
  ∀ κ : ZMod n → ℝ, DiscreteFourVertexPos κ → RealizesR2 κ

blocks.title: The extrema form of the hypothesis class

blocks.tex:
Everything above hypothesizes a \emph{level}: $\mathrm{DFV}(\kappa; c)$ asks
for a real number $c$ and four cyclically ordered indices whose values
alternate across it (\cref{def:discrete_fourvertex}).  Dahlberg and
Tabachnikov hypothesize instead an \emph{extremum count}: at least two local
maxima and at least two local minima of the curvature, in the plateau-aware
sense.

The two hypotheses are \emph{a priori} different, and the development has so
far only proved one implication between them: the level form implies the
extremum form (\cref{cor:dfv_plateau_extrema_window}).  This section proves
the missing implication, and hence that the two hypothesis classes coincide
exactly --- no adjacent-inequality caveat, no plateau caveat.  The
consequence is that $\mathrm{TP2}(n)$ (\cref{def:tab_problem2}), stated in
the level form, is \emph{equivalent} to the same statement in Dahlberg's
extremum form, so the chapter's central object really is the literature's
problem and not a value-separated proxy for it.

\medskip

Note that Dahlberg's ``$P$ is a local maximum'' is exactly
$\mathrm{PlateauMaxRun}$ (\cref{def:plateau_max_run}): $I(f,P)$ is the
maximal constant interval through $P$ (our lifted run $a, \dots, a+k$), and
the defining inequality is the strict drop at the two extended ends
$P_{j-1}, P_{k+1}$ (our $f(a-1) < f(a)$ and $f(a+k+1) < f(a)$).  His two
extreme points are \emph{distinct} exactly when the two runs are disjoint as
sets of residues, which is the disjointness clause below.

blocks.label: def:tab_two_max_runs
blocks.title: two distinct plateau maxima
blocks.body:
$\mathrm{HasTwoPlateauMaxRuns}\,\kappa$ holds when there are $\mathbb{N}$-lifts
  $a_1, k_1, a_2, k_2$ with $k_1 < n$, $k_2 < n$,
  $\mathrm{PlateauMaxRun}\,\kappa\,a_1\,k_1$,
  $\mathrm{PlateauMaxRun}\,\kappa\,a_2\,k_2$, and the two runs disjoint as
  residues: $(a_1 + m_1) \ne (a_2 + m_2)$ in $\ZMod n$ for all $m_1 \le k_1$
  and $m_2 \le k_2$.  This is Dahlberg's ``$\kappa$ has at least two distinct
  local maxima'', transcribed.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HasTwoPlateauMaxRuns
lean.code:
def HasTwoPlateauMaxRuns (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ : ℕ, k₁ < n ∧ k₂ < n ∧
    PlateauMaxRun κ a₁ k₁ ∧ PlateauMaxRun κ a₂ k₂ ∧
    ∀ m₁, m₁ ≤ k₁ → ∀ m₂, m₂ ≤ k₂ →
      ((a₁ + m₁ : ℕ) : ZMod n) ≠ ((a₂ + m₂ : ℕ) : ZMod n)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HasTwoPlateauMinRuns
lean.code:
def HasTwoPlateauMinRuns (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ : ℕ, k₁ < n ∧ k₂ < n ∧
    PlateauMinRun κ a₁ k₁ ∧ PlateauMinRun κ a₂ k₂ ∧
    ∀ m₁, m₁ ≤ k₁ → ∀ m₂, m₂ ≤ k₂ →
      ((a₁ + m₁ : ℕ) : ZMod n) ≠ ((a₂ + m₂ : ℕ) : ZMod n)

blocks.label: def:tab_extrema_class
blocks.title: the extremum-form hypothesis class
blocks.body:
$\mathrm{DiscreteFourVertexExtrema}\,\kappa$ holds when $\kappa_i > 0$ for
  all $i$ and either $\kappa$ is constant, or $\kappa$ has two distinct
  plateau maxima \emph{and} two distinct plateau minima.  This is the
  positive-curvature form of the conclusion class of Dahlberg's Theorem 1,
  used as a hypothesis.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.DiscreteFourVertexExtrema

blocks.label: lem:tab_dfv_level_pos
blocks.title: a window level of a positive profile is positive
blocks.body: If $\mathrm{DFV}(\kappa; c)$ and $\kappa_i > 0$ for all $i$, then $c > 0$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.DFV.pos_of_pos
lean.code:
theorem DFV.pos_of_pos {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ} (h : DFV κ c)
    (hpos : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) : 0 < c := by
  obtain ⟨_, i₂, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, h2, _, _⟩ := h
  exact lt_trans (hpos ((i₂ : ℕ) : ZMod n)) h2

blocks.tex:
The window supplies an index $i_2$ with $\kappa_{i_2} < c$, and
  $0 < \kappa_{i_2}$ by hypothesis.

The heart of the section is the following.  It says something slightly
stronger than ``two maxima and two minima give a level'': \emph{two maxima
alone already give a level}, and the level can be read off from the
\emph{smaller} of the two maxima together with its own two immediate
neighbours.  No minimum is ever inspected.

blocks.label: thm:tab_dfv_of_two_max_runs
blocks.title: two distinct plateau maxima produce a window level
blocks.body:
Let $n \ne 0$ and let $\kappa : \ZMod n \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy
  $\mathrm{HasTwoPlateauMaxRuns}\,\kappa$.  Then $\mathrm{DFV}(\kappa; c)$
  holds for some $c$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.exists_dfv_of_two_plateauMaxRun
lean.code:
theorem exists_dfv_of_two_plateauMaxRun [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (h : HasTwoPlateauMaxRuns κ) : ∃ c, DFV κ c := by
  obtain ⟨a₁, k₁, a₂, k₂, -, -, h₁, h₂, hdisj⟩ := h
  rcases le_total (κ (a₁ : ZMod n)) (κ (a₂ : ZMod n)) with hle | hle
  · exact exists_dfv_of_two_plateauMaxRun_aux h₁ hdisj hle
  · exact exists_dfv_of_two_plateauMaxRun_aux h₂
      (fun m₂ hm₂ m₁ hm₁ => (hdisj m₁ hm₁ m₂ hm₂).symm) hle

blocks.tex:
Write the two runs as $(a_1, k_1)$ and $(a_2, k_2)$, with values
  $v_1 = \kappa(a_1)$ and $v_2 = \kappa(a_2)$ (the value is constant along
  each run).  The statement is symmetric in the two runs, so assume
  $v_1 \le v_2$; otherwise swap them, which also swaps the two sides of the
  disjointness clause.  So the first run is the \emph{lower} of the two
  maxima, and it is the one that fixes the level.

  \emph{Step 1: locate the second run.}  Since $n \ne 0$ we may set
  $d = (a_2 - a_1)^{\mathrm{val}} \in \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, the unique such
  lift with $(a_1 + d) = a_2$ in $\ZMod n$.  We claim
  \[
    k_1 + 1 \;<\; d \;<\; n - 1 .
  \]
  \begin{itemize}
    \item $d > k_1$: for each $m \le k_1$ the disjointness clause (taken at
      $m_2 = 0$) gives $(a_1 + m) \ne a_2$ in $\ZMod n$, i.e.\ $m \ne d$
      because both $m \le k_1 < n$ and $d < n$ are $\mathbb{N}$-lifts below
      $n$.  Hence $d \notin \{0, \dots, k_1\}$.
    \item $d \ne k_1 + 1$: the run hypothesis gives
      $\kappa(a_1 + k_1 + 1) < v_1$.  If $d$ were $k_1 + 1$ then
      $a_2 = (a_1 + k_1 + 1)$ in $\ZMod n$ and this would read
      $v_2 < v_1 \le v_2$.
    \item $d \ne n - 1$: since $n \ne 0$, the residue of $a_1 + (n-1)$ is
      $a_1 - 1$, and the run hypothesis gives $\kappa(a_1 - 1) < v_1$.  If
      $d$ were $n-1$ then $a_2 = a_1 - 1$ and again $v_2 < v_1 \le v_2$.
      Together with $d \le n-1$ this gives $d < n-1$.
  \end{itemize}

  \emph{Step 2: the level.}  Put
  \[
    M \;=\; \max\bigl(\kappa(a_1 - 1),\ \kappa(a_1 + k_1 + 1)\bigr),
    \qquad
    c \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\,(M + v_1).
  \]
  Both arguments of the max are $< v_1$ by the run hypothesis, so $M < v_1$
  and therefore $M < c < v_1$.

  \emph{Step 3: the window.}  Take the four $\mathbb{N}$-lifts
  \[
    i_1 = a_1, \qquad i_2 = a_1 + k_1 + 1, \qquad i_3 = a_1 + d,
    \qquad i_4 = a_1 + (n-1).
  \]
  They are cyclically ordered, $i_1 < i_2 < i_3 < i_4 < i_1 + n$: the first
  inequality is trivial, the second and third are Step 1, and the last holds
  because $n \ne 0$.  Their residues are $a_1$, $a_1 + k_1 + 1$, $a_2$ and
  $a_1 - 1$, so the four level inequalities are
  \[
    c < v_1, \qquad \kappa(a_1 + k_1 + 1) \le M < c, \qquad
    c < v_1 \le v_2, \qquad \kappa(a_1 - 1) \le M < c,
  \]
  all established in Step 2.  This is exactly $\mathrm{DFV}(\kappa; c)$.

blocks.label: thm:tab_pos_iff_extrema
blocks.title: the level form and the extremum form define the same class

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.discreteFourVertexPos_iff_extrema
lean.code:
theorem discreteFourVertexPos_iff_extrema [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} :
    DiscreteFourVertexPos κ ↔ DiscreteFourVertexExtrema κ := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hpos, hconst | ⟨c, -, hdfv⟩⟩
    · exact ⟨hpos, Or.inl hconst⟩
    · exact ⟨hpos, Or.inr ⟨hdfv.plateau_extrema.1, hdfv.plateau_extrema.2⟩⟩
  · rintro ⟨hpos, hconst | ⟨hmax, -⟩⟩
    · exact ⟨hpos, Or.inl hconst⟩
    · obtain ⟨c, hdfv⟩ := exists_dfv_of_two_plateauMaxRun hmax
      exact ⟨hpos, Or.inr ⟨c, hdfv.pos_of_pos hpos, hdfv⟩⟩

deps.title: the DFV window meets Dahlberg's conclusion class --- wrapped form
deps.label: cor:dfv_plateau_extrema_window

blocks.tex:
Both sides carry the same positivity clause, so only the disjunction moves,
  and the constant disjunct is literally shared.

  ($\Rightarrow$)  In the window disjunct we have $c > 0$ with
  $\mathrm{DFV}(\kappa; c)$; \cref{cor:dfv_plateau_extrema_window} returns
  two disjoint plateau maximum runs and two disjoint plateau minimum runs,
  each with run length $< n$ --- exactly
  $\mathrm{HasTwoPlateauMaxRuns}\,\kappa \wedge
   \mathrm{HasTwoPlateauMinRuns}\,\kappa$.

  ($\Leftarrow$)  In the extremum disjunct, discard the minimum runs and feed
  the maximum runs to \cref{thm:tab_dfv_of_two_max_runs}, obtaining $c$ with
  $\mathrm{DFV}(\kappa; c)$.  By \cref{lem:tab_dfv_level_pos} and positivity
  this $c$ is automatically positive, which is what the right disjunct of
  $\mathrm{DiscreteFourVertexPos}$ demands.

blocks.label: cor:tab_problem2_extrema_form
blocks.title: Problem 2 in Dahlberg's extremum form
blocks.body:
For $n \ne 0$,
  \[
    \mathrm{TP2}(n)
    \iff
    \bigl(\forall \kappa,\ \mathrm{DiscreteFourVertexExtrema}\,\kappa
      \Rightarrow \mathrm{RealizesR2}\,\kappa \bigr).
  \]
  So the named proposition of this chapter is the literature's problem, not a
  value-separated approximation to it.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.tabachnikovProblem2_iff_extrema_form
lean.code:
theorem tabachnikovProblem2_iff_extrema_form [NeZero n] :
    TabachnikovProblem2 n ↔
      ∀ κ : ZMod n → ℝ, DiscreteFourVertexExtrema κ → RealizesR2 κ := by
  constructor
  · exact fun h κ hκ => h κ (discreteFourVertexPos_iff_extrema.mpr hκ)
  · exact fun h κ hκ => h κ (discreteFourVertexPos_iff_extrema.mp hκ)
